title: Rate limits & Org/Project Keys demo with HarborPoint Health

Next steps agreed: send pricing, SOC2 and network diagrams, provision trial org and project keys, schedule benchmark run vs current hosted endpoints.

Security: SSO, KMS, audit logs, SOC2

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Reed (Redwood SE), Dr. Lisa Morgan (CTO - HarborPoint), Rahul Desai (Head of ML Ops), Marta Lopez (Sec Eng)

Summary (auto): Ava gave a live walkthrough of Redwood Console rate limits, org and project keys for multi-tenant controls, Daniel did a quick demo of enforcement and telemetry in the Console and API. Questions on Dedicated/private enforcement, SSO/SAML, KMS, and contractual SLAs.

00:00:05 - Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava from Redwood, and with me is Daniel our solutions engineer. Quick introductions?
00:00:18 - Lisa: Hi, Lisa Morgan, CTO at HarborPoint. We run a mixed cloud/on-prem deployment for sensitive patient pipelines.
00:00:25 - Rahul: Rahul Desai, ML Ops. We handle model inference pipelines and scaling.
00:00:28 - Marta: Marta Lopez, security. I'll be focused on encryption, audit logs and controls.
00:00:35 - Ava: Great, thanks. Today we'll focus on rate limits, quotas, and how org and project keys let you partition tenants and control spend. We'll show Console + API flows and talk about Dedicated and Private implications.

00:01:05 - Daniel: I'll kick off with the Console demo, show how a trial org is set up, creating projects, issuing project keys, and where rate limits live.
00:01:22 - Ava: Quick context question: what's your main pain with the current system? Is it noisy noisy rate spikes, or lack of per-tenant visibility?
00:01:30 - Rahul: A bit of both. Right now we use a homegrown proxy and we can't easily set per-customer token budgets or spike protection without big infra work. We also want clear billing attribution.
00:01:45 - Lisa: Also we have compliance constraints; some partners require data never leaves our VPC so curious about private deployment enforcement.

00:02:12 - Daniel: Okay, demo time. (keyboard sounds) I'm in the Redwood Console. Top-left, you can see the org view. Under org settings -> Keys, you can create org-level keys and project keys. We typically recommend one org key for infra and project keys per product or customer for isolation.
00:02:34 - Daniel: Creating a project, call it harborpoint-dev. Add quota policy — we can set token per-minute, concurrent requests, and monthly token budget.
00:02:47 - Daniel: Example: set a per-project QPS of 50, burst up to 200, and a hard monthly cap of 5M tokens. Those are enforced at the gateway.
00:03:05 - Rahul: When you say enforced at the gateway, is that the Redwood hosted gateway or in Dedicated/private there's a local gateway?
00:03:12 - Daniel: Good question. For hosted, enforcement is in our hosted edge layer. For Dedicated, we deploy a dedicated gateway in your VPC or cluster that enforces the same policies. For Private/on-prem, you run the control plane that pushes rules to local proxies — enforcement stays local. There might be slight differences in telemetry latency but policy parity is the goal.
00:03:45 - Marta: How do you authenticate project keys? Are they JWTs? How do they tie into SSO and RBAC?
00:03:52 - Ava: Project keys are secure tokens you can rotate. For enterprise, we support SSO/SAML and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC. Keys are independent from SSO — service-to-service keys — but you can map team-level permissions to projects. Keys are stored encrypted at rest; we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private.
00:04:20 - Marta: Customer-managed KMS, that helps. Do audit logs include key usage and request payload metadata?
00:04:28 - Daniel: Yes, audit trails show key usage, timestamps, model invoked, token counts, and response codes. Payloads are redacted by default unless you opt-in for debug-level logs (not recommended for PHI). Logs can be exported to your SIEM via secure forwarding.
00:04:52 - Lisa: Can you do per-tenant cost alerts? Eg, if a particular customer is burning through tokens, we want an alert and automatic throttling or sandboxing.
00:05:00 - Daniel: Yep, Console supports alerting on token burn rates per project and we have automatic soft-and-hard throttles. Soft throttle sends 429 warnings, hard throttle blocks until an admin increases quota or the window resets. You can also set up automated webhooks to notify your billing system.
00:05:22 - Rahul: What about multi-model fallbacks? If a large request hits and primary model is expensive, can we route to a cheaper variant automatically? That ties into cost controls.
00:05:31 - Ava: Absolutely — routing policies can route by cost tier or latency SLO. You can set fallback chains; those are independent of rate limits but work in tandem. For ex, when budget threshold hits we can automatically route to a quantized variant or smaller model.

00:06:10 - (noise) Daniel: Now I'll show the API flow. In Postman, you supply the project key in the Authorization header. The endpoint returns standard response plus rate-limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and a per-project usage token header.
00:06:31 - Daniel: If you exceed the soft limit, we'll return 429 with a Retry-After header. For extended bursts we apply token bucket semantics.
00:06:45 - Lisa: Is there a way to simulate load to see how throttles will behave?
00:06:49 - Daniel: Yes, we include a benchmark harness and we'll provide a runner script. Also if you want, we can run a managed benchmark from Redwood on your Dedicated cluster during the trial — it's one of the next steps.

00:07:20 - Rahul: For the Dedicated option, how do we limit cross-project noisy neighbor effects?
00:07:26 - Daniel: Dedicated supports isolate pools and per-project assignment to GPU pools. We do kernel-level isolation via dedicated queues and KV cache partitioning. In practice you can pin heavy tenants to their own capacity pool. There's also autoscaling policies to ensure one project can't starve others.
00:07:48 - Marta: Any constraints for private/on-prem? If we run an air-gapped instance, can we still get usage reports in your cloud console?
00:07:56 - Ava: For fully air-gapped, telemetry stays local; we provide a private console bundle or a reporting agent that can export batched telemetry over approved channels. For VPC deployments we can set up secure peering to push telemetry to your logging endpoints.

00:08:25 - Lisa: Security question: SOC two and penetration testing?
00:08:30 - Ava: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we'll share the report under NDA. For Dedicated and Private we also provide more detailed configs and can support customer-led or third-party pen tests.
00:08:44 - Marta: Good. Does Redwood support bringing-your-own-keys (BYOK) for model artifacts and logs?
00:08:50 - Daniel: For Dedicated/Private, yes — BYOK for encryption at rest via your KMS/HSM. For hosted, we offer dedicated key support for enterprise customers.

00:09:18 - Rahul: About quotas: do you support hierarchical quota (org-level + project-level) with inheritance and overrides?
00:09:25 - Daniel: Yes. Org-level caps provide a global guardrail and individual projects inherit defaults but can have stricter or more permissive overrides depending on role/approval. We also have org-level burn alerts and per-project rate limiting.

00:09:52 - Ava: Let's walk through a common flow: create org, create two projects (api-ingest, partner-portal), assign project keys, set monthly caps and per-minute QPS. Then instrument the SDK to report token usage back to the admin dashboard.
00:10:10 - (typing) Daniel: Adding a webhook integration to forward usage events to your billing system. You can also export CSVs for month-end reconciliations.

00:10:38 - Lisa: If we run a pilot, what are recommended success metrics? Latency P95 under X ms, cost per 1k tokens, and no data egress violations.
00:10:47 - Ava: Exactly — typical pilot metrics we use: average token cost, percent requests served within latency SLOs, throttling events, and billing attribution accuracy. We'll help define those in the pilot SOW.

00:11:20 - Rahul: Can we enforce content filtering per project? Some partners require stricter moderation.
00:11:26 - Daniel: Yes, you can attach policy chains per project. Filtering and moderation hooks can be applied at the gateway, and you can configure different thresholds per project.

00:12:02 - Marta: A practical: If a rogue script starts spamming tokens, how do we do emergency lockdowns?
00:12:09 - Ava: Console supports immediate key revocation, suspend project, and an emergency global throttle. We can also automate policies that suspend keys after N errors or after hitting a certain throttle pattern.

00:12:36 - Lisa: Pricing ask: can you give a sample for Hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity? We have 10M tokens/month baseline and spikes up to 30M.
00:12:45 - Ava: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet. Roughly: hosted pay-as-you-go per token; Dedicated you commit to reserved GPU pools with a monthly minimum; pricing depends on model family and utilization. We'll include sample numbers for 10M baseline and additional overage.

00:13:10 - Rahul: Regarding rate-limit headers, can we surface per-tenant budgets to end-users so our app shows 'X tokens left this month'?
00:13:18 - Daniel: You can. The header plus a usage API lets you build a UI to show per-customer budgets. Many customers do that for transparency.

00:13:45 - Ava: Quick note: we'll provision a trial org with two project keys — dev and test — so you can try project-level caps and the SDK. Expect keys by tomorrow.

00:14:02 - Marta: About data residency: our EU partners require their requests to route to EU-only regions. Can per-project routing enforce region residency?
00:14:11 - Daniel: Yes, routing policies can pin projects to regions. For Dedicated/Private you can deploy region-specific pools and policies ensure requests for that project only hit EU pools.

00:14:38 - Lisa: Any gotchas for migrating from our proxy? We have JWT-based auth today.
00:14:45 - Daniel: We provide an adapter pattern and a migration checklist. The proxy can keep authenticating JWTs and map them to Redwood project keys; we also support token exchange flows to minimize code changes.

00:15:10 - (slight crosstalk) Ava: We'll share the migration doc and the sample nginx adapter we've used with other customers.

00:15:30 - Rahul: Is there built-in cost forecasting by project? We want to estimate month-end costs if usage trends continue.
00:15:36 - Daniel: Yes, Console has a forecasting module that extrapolates current burn rate and gives alerts if you cross thresholds. It also simulates policy changes like reducing QPS to see cost impact.

00:16:05 - Marta: For audit readiness, can we get streaming logs to our Splunk instance with identities mapped to project keys?
00:16:12 - Daniel: Absolutely, we support log forwarding, structured events with project key ID, model, token count, and redacted payloads.

00:16:38 - Ava: Let's jump back to the demo — I'll show the rate limit policy editor. (mouse clicks) Here you can add a soft limit, hard limit, burst window, and a webhook action on threshold.
00:16:56 - Daniel: Adding a rule: if monthly budget > 90% then trigger a webhook to billing; also we can attach automated fallback routing to cheaper model.

00:17:22 - Lisa: Perfect. For the pilot, we'd want the webhook to call our billing microservice and to auto-suspend keys when over budget pending review.
00:17:30 - Ava: That's doable. We'll include that in the pilot configuration.

00:17:45 - Rahul: Any latency overhead from enforcing per-project quotas?
00:17:50 - Daniel: Minimal — enforcement happens at the edge gateway with highly optimized path. For hosted it's <2ms added median overhead; Dedicated in-VPC similar numbers, depending on network topology. If you're running on-prem with heavy network NATing it might be slightly higher. We'll run benchmarks.

00:18:18 - Marta: Do you support per-API-key rate-limiting as well as per-project?
00:18:23 - Daniel: Yes, hierarchy is flexible: api-key -> project -> org. You can set limits at any level and combine them.

00:18:45 - (pause) Ava: We take questions about regulatory controls — anything else on that front?
00:18:50 - Marta: Just one: do logs contain PII? If so, how do you manage retention?
00:18:57 - Daniel: Payloads are redacted by default but if you opt-in to store them we recommend short retention windows and encryption under your KMS. Retention policies are configurable per project.

00:19:20 - Lisa: For the pilot timeline, we were thinking 4 weeks. Does that fit your typical pilot?
00:19:26 - Ava: 4 weeks is common. Week 1: provision + basic tests. Week 2: benchmarking and tuning. Week 3: integration and alerting. Week 4: evaluation and results. We'll propose a SOW with milestones.

00:19:50 - Rahul: Does Redwood provide any assistance migrating our existing policy logic into your rule editor?
00:19:55 - Daniel: Yes, Solutions Engineering helps with the first pass and we hand off scripts and IaC templates.

00:20:12 - Ava: I'll put some links in the follow-up: sample migration doc, benchmark harness repo, rate-limit policy guide.

00:20:25 - Marta: On legal: do you have a standard DPA and model for data processing addendum?
00:20:31 - Ava: Yes, standard DPA and data residency add-ons. We'll have Legal send the DPA and SOC2 under NDA.

00:20:48 - (brief silence) Daniel: Quick note: API responses include X-Model-Variant header which helps you measure how often fallbacks are used. That ties into Optimize recommendations.
00:20:58 - Rahul: Nice. On Optimize: can it recommend quantization profiles per workload that respect latency SLOs?
00:21:04 - Daniel: Yes, Optimize looks at sequence length distributions, p95 latency and recommends model variants and quantization that trade cost vs quality. We'll include Optimize recommendations in the benchmark report.

00:21:30 - Lisa: Great. Any concerns about vendor lock-in? If we move away, can we export project configs?
00:21:36 - Ava: You can export policies, keys mapping, and usage reports. Our goal is to make the migration path clear — we provide IaC and JSON exports.

00:22:02 - Marta: For Dedicated, what SLA do you offer for rate-limit enforcement and uptime?
00:22:08 - Ava: Dedicated comes with SLA backed targets for availability and latency tiers. Exact SLA depends on commit level; we'll include SLA options in the pricing packet.

00:22:30 - Rahul: Ok, last technical — how do you handle KV cache when different projects hit large context windows?
00:22:37 - Daniel: We partition KV cache by project and use efficient eviction policies. For large context workloads you can use per-project cache-size quotas or pin warm sessions to dedicated pools.

00:22:58 - (typing) Ava: We're approaching the middle of the call — let's recap next steps.
00:23:05 - Ava: Action items: we'll send pricing + DPA + SOC2, provision trial org + keys, Daniel will share benchmark checklist. Marta will forward required security questionnaires.
00:23:18 - Lisa: Sounds good. Please include sample numbers for Dedicated reserved capacity with 10M baseline and 30M peak.
00:23:25 - Ava: Will do.
00:23:40 - Daniel: One final demo bit — showing realtime usage metrics for a project. (click) You can see token consumption, alert triggers, and model fallbacks in the timeline.
00:24:00 - Rahul: That's useful. Can the timeline be filtered by user or session id?
00:24:05 - Daniel: Yes, filtering by session_id, user_id, or request_id is supported if you pass those identifiers in the request metadata.
00:24:22 - Marta: Any rate-limit behavior differences when using streaming APIs vs non-streaming?
00:24:28 - Daniel: Streaming consumes tokens similarly; we account per token produced. The main difference is latency characteristics and how you set concurrent stream limits.
00:24:50 - (brief pause) Ava: Ok, unless there are more questions, we'll close with next steps and send materials.
00:24:58 - Lisa: No more questions for now. Thanks, this was helpful.
00:25:05 - Rahul: Thanks Ava and Daniel.
00:25:09 - Marta: Thanks. We'll review the security docs once received.
00:25:25 - Ava: Great — recap: pricing + SOC2 + DPA + migration docs + benchmark harness + trial org keys. We'll target sending the keys by 2026-07-23 and pricing by 2026-07-24. Schedule benchmark for week of 2026-07-27.
00:25:45 - Daniel: I'll email the checklist and script.
00:25:50 - Lisa: Looking forward to the trial.
00:25:55 - Ava: Thanks everyone.
00:26:02 - (call wraps, small chatter)
